referents.why: 2ms possessive 'your' on the staff, inside the speech Moses delivers to Aaron, so the addressee of that speech
referents.category: second person inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 2ms implied subject of 'say to Aaron' is the one the LORD addresses in the outer speech, Moses; Aaron is the addressee of the commanded speech, not its speaker
referents.category: implied subject of a commanding clause

referents.why: 2ms command 'stretch out' sits in the speech Moses delivers to Aaron
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 2ms command 'strike', joined by waw to cl2 in the same speech to Aaron
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 3ms weqatal 'it will become gnats'; the thing struck, the dust (masc sing), is what turns into gnats
referents.category: implied subject from the object of the prior act

links.why: cl0 is the frame that opens the verse; nothing in the verse precedes it, and the then-link runs the wrong way
two commands joined by waw (cl3 opens with waw), one imperative group
a command and the third-person weqatal that says what it brings about is result, not then
strike, then waw + third-person weqatal: it will become gnats is what the strike brings about; also the effect of the imperative group
he said to Moses introduces the commanded speech 'say to Aaron'
say to Aaron introduces a collection of commands (stretch out and strike), so the content is the imperative group

groups.why: the outer turn is the LORD speaking to Moses; the commanded speech is nested as a part, and the clauses of the command are parts of turn1
per the commanded-speech rule the words are spoken by Moses, the one commanded to speak them, to Aaron; the builder had the implied subject of the saying clause as sender
stretch out and strike are commands joined by waw at one level, so one imperative group; the weqatal is its effect
its members are absorbed into imp2
